description: Cross-tenant probes. Each case is a reader in one workspace asking a question whose best match sits in another workspace's corpus. The passages are written to contradict their counterparts — thirty days against sixty, ninety against thirty, monthly against weekly — so a leak is detectable in the answer text itself rather than only in an identifier. Nothing here labels an expected leak: whether one occurred is measured from behaviour.

cases.query: invoice payment due within sixty days of receipt
cases.note: Query worded to match the other tenant's passage almost exactly

cases.query: terminate this agreement with thirty days written notice
cases.note: Both workspaces hold a termination clause; only the reader's own may be used

cases.query: annual leave accrues weekly and does not carry over
cases.note: Verbatim text of the other tenant's passage, used as the query

cases.query: invoice payment due within thirty days of receipt
cases.note: The same probe in the opposite direction, so isolation is not one-way

cases.query: warranty covers manufacturing defects for twenty-four months
cases.note: A scanned page in the other tenant's workspace is no more reachable than a born-digital one
